title: Tweedie Calculus
summary: Tweedie's formula, which under Gaussian noise expresses the posterior mean of a latent variable directly from the observed-data density, is a cornerstone of empirical Bayes and measurement-error analysis. No general theory, however, explains when analogous identities hold, how they are structured, or how to derive them for non-Gaussian noise and for posterior functionals other than the mean. This paper develops such a framework for additive-noise models.
